title: Recall Check Before Sign-Up
what: Let a visitor type a brand and model (or snap a label) and instantly see if it has an open recall, free. It proves the Recall Tracking promise on the first screen and is the kind of hook people share.
before: Recall Tracking is one line on the home page
after: 'Check Your Water Heater for Recalls' tool, then 'Track All My Equipment' button

title: Snap a Label, Auto-Fill the Model and Serial
what: On the photo step, read the brand, model and serial from the label photo and show them back for a quick confirm. Fewer typing steps, and the quote gets exact equipment data.
after: Photo, then 'Rheem XG50T, Serial 0423...' with Looks Right / Fix It

title: Add Visits to My Calendar
what: On the confirmation screen, offer an .ics download (or Google Calendar link) for the first visit and the seasonal schedule. Members stop forgetting visits and no-shows drop.
after: 'Add My Visit Schedule to Calendar' button with 4 seasonal events

title: Fix the Silver vs Platinum Mismatch
what: The video's closing card shows $99 Silver and $219 Gold, but the app offers Gold and Platinum at thousands a year. Pick one lineup (the research suggests Silver, Gold, Platinum) and make the video and app match.
before: Video: $99 Silver, $219 Gold. App: Gold $2,780+, Platinum
after: One lineup everywhere, same names and prices

title: Add a Silver Entry Tier
what: The pricing research shows Gold at $2,600+ is a big first purchase; a 2-visit Silver at about $900 to $1,300 gets you into the house and the visit report sells the upgrade.
after: Silver, Gold (Most Popular), Platinum cards

title: Show Monthly Price First
what: Lead with 'About $232 a month' and put the yearly total underneath, and let Gold be paid monthly or quarterly too. Big annual numbers scare people off at the moment they decide.
after: $232 / month, billed monthly (or $2,780 a year)

title: Write Clear Cancellation Terms
what: The agreement says cancellation and refund terms are to be determined. State them plainly (for example, cancel anytime before the next visit, prorated refund) and show a one-line version next to the price.
before: 'Cancellation and refund terms are to be determined.'
after: 'Cancel anytime. Unused visits refunded.' under each price

title: Finalize the Agreement and Waiver
what: Both are marked Draft, Pending Legal Review. Get them reviewed and swap in final text before taking real sign-ups, since a draft label right before signing kills trust.
before: Two DRAFT boxes and two signatures
after: One final agreement, one signature, a summary of key terms

title: Turn On Real Payments
what: The payment fields are disabled with a 'Demo' note, so nobody can actually buy. Wire up Stripe Checkout (or a 'Reserve Now, Pay at First Visit' option) so the funnel converts.
after: Stripe Checkout or 'Reserve My Spot, Pay After First Visit'

title: Collect a Waitlist for Out-of-Area ZIPs
what: A ZIP like 90210 only gets a warning and then a metro Detroit estimate that means nothing. Instead say 'We are not there yet' and capture an email so you know where demand is.
before: Warning, then 'tap Next again to continue'
after: 'Not in your area yet. Want a heads-up when we are?' + email

title: Hide the Prototype Badge
what: The header says 'Prototype, Draft Pricing' on every screen. For real homeowners, drop it and keep the 'estimate' wording near the price instead.
before: 'PROTOTYPE, DRAFT PRICING' tag in the header
after: Clean header with logo and a Call or Text button

title: Don't Auto-Open the Video
what: The explainer opens in a full-screen modal on first visit and downloads a 4 MB video before people see anything. Show the page first, with a poster card that plays the video on tap.
before: Modal video covers the home page
after: Hero with a small 'Watch 60s Video' poster thumbnail

title: Add Real Trust Signals
what: Show license and insurance numbers, a named local owner, reviews or a 'Founding Member' count, and a satisfaction guarantee near the Get Started button. Today the claims have no proof.
after: License #, insurer, '4.9 stars from 31 neighbors', guarantee badge

title: Add a Call or Text Us Button
what: There is no phone number or contact anywhere. A sticky Text Us button gives nervous buyers a human and catches leads who won't fill a form.
after: 'Questions? Text Us' in the header and on the price screen

title: Explain Unsure Answers on the Price
what: After 8 Unsure answers the price quietly assumes a typical home. Show which answers were guessed with a one-tap fix, so the price feels honest rather than random.
after: List: 'Furnaces: guessed 1, Fix' for each Unsure

title: Show a Price Range While Answering
what: Show a small running estimate (for example $2,400 to $3,200) that narrows as they answer. It rewards each answer and avoids sticker shock at the end.
after: Sticky 'Your estimate so far: $2.4k to $3.2k' bar

title: Shorter Path: Skip Straight to a Price
what: Offer 'Just Give Me a Ballpark' after the ZIP and home size, filling the rest with typical values. Impatient visitors still see a number and can refine later.
after: ZIP + size, then 'See Ballpark' or 'Refine My Price'

title: Save Progress and Email the Quote
what: Let people email themselves the estimate or get a resume link. Most homeowners decide with a spouse, so they need to come back later.
after: 'Email Me This Quote' button on the price screen

title: Spell Out What a Visit Looks Like
what: Add a simple timeline: 'Fall visit: furnace tune-up, gutter clean, smoke and CO test, 90 minutes'. People buy what they can picture.
after: 4 season cards with what happens and how long

title: Compare Against Booking It Yourself
what: Show 'What this costs a la carte in metro Detroit' next to the membership price, using the research numbers. It frames the membership as savings, but only if the numbers truly hold up.
after: 'Booked separately: about $3,400. With Gold: $2,780.'

title: Make the Signature Step Lighter
what: Two separate draw-or-type signatures plus two checkboxes is a lot on a phone. Use one combined 'I agree to the Agreement and Waiver' checkbox with a typed name.
after: 1 checkbox + typed full name

title: Label Every Form Field for Screen Readers
what: Five inputs on the sign-up step (typed signatures and card fields) have no linked label. Add proper labels and error announcements so screen readers and autofill work.
after: All inputs labelled, autocomplete set (name, tel, email, street-address)

title: Add to Home Screen After Sign-Up
what: After joining, offer a small dismissible 'Keep Smart Upkeep on your phone' card, so members can see their schedule and reports like an app.
after: Dismissible install card with Add / Not Now

title: Offline Shutoffs and Emergency Info for Members
what: After the first visit, give members a page with photos of their own water, gas and electric shutoffs that works offline. It is useful on the worst day and makes the membership sticky.
before: Shutoff valves checked, not recorded for the owner
after: 'My Shutoffs' page with photos and steps, works offline

title: A Sample Visit Report
what: Link a sample written report (photos, findings, next steps) from the price screen. It shows the value of 'Written report after every visit' better than a bullet.
after: 'See a Sample Report' link opens a 1-page example

title: Seasonal Reminders by Text
what: Text members a day before each visit and a short tip each season (for example 'Change your furnace filter'). It keeps the brand top of mind and cuts no-shows.
after: Opt-in SMS checkbox at sign-up

title: Referral Credit
what: Give a credit (for example one free month) for each neighbor who joins. Home services spread by word of mouth in a neighborhood.
after: 'Share With a Neighbor, Both Get a Month Free' on confirmation
